steps: Pressure cook the soaked chickpeas with the bay leaf in fresh water until they mash easily.
Heat the oil and fry the onion until golden.
Add most of the ginger, the garlic and the green chilli and stir for a minute.
Add the tomato and salt and cook until it breaks down.
Stir in the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin and garam masala until fragrant.
Pour in the chickpeas with their cooking water, mash a few, and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until thick.
Take out the bay leaf and crush in the kasuri methi.
Fry the last of the ginger in hot ghee, pour it over the chole and add the coriander leaves.
note: Sources use 50 to 80 g of dry chickpeas a person; 60 g makes a good bowl next to roti or rice. Lemon is gone because none of the sources use it; they get their sourness from amchur.
